newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka poll group alleges rigging, intimidation.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka poll group alleges rigging, intimidation.

text.p: An independent Sri Lankan election monitoring group said on Monday there was widespread intimidation and vote fraud in last week's local government elections, which the ruling coalition won by a landslide.

"We believe that the level of violence on election day and the magnitude of impersonations were such as to affect the result of the election in a number of local authorities," said the Movement for Free and Fair Election.
Impersonation refers to the casting of votes by people using another voters' ballot papers.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga's ruling People's Alliance (PA) coalition won 194 of the 238 local councils at stake in last Friday's poll.
The main opposition United National Party (UNP) won 43 while one council was won by an independent group.
Former prime minister and UNP leader Ranil Wickremesinghe has accused the government of vote-rigging and intimidating voters into casting ballots for the ruling coalition.

"If not for the intimidation and rigging, the result would have been a photo finish," he told a news conference on Sunday. President Kumaratunga said in a statement on Sunday that the poll was free and fair.

The Movement for Free and Fair Election said that although leaders of all parties said they opposed violence, they failed to respond to calls to remove from the campaign those responsible for acts of violence.
"The response to this was an embarrassed silence: no political party took any meaningful action to demonstrate unequivocally their rejection of violence," it said in a statement.
The independent Centre for Monitoring Election Violence said it had recorded about 200 incidents of poll-related violence last Thursday and Friday alone.

"We consider that all political parties, and particularly the PA and the UNP, have been seriously remiss in taking effective steps to eradicate the violence which has increasingly vitiated the democratic process," it said.
The monitoring group also accused the government of manipulating state media for its own benefit in the campaign.

"The government's control of the state-owned electronic media was manifestly abused to the benefit of the PA," it said. "Election rallies attended by the president were given extended coverage, with opposition groups given much less attention."
The state media continued plugging the PA even after campaigning officially closed, it said.
